plan_a_advantages: Includes a dedicated aerobic session for endurance building.
Offers a longer workout duration (225 minutes vs. 179 minutes) providing more opportunity for physiological adaptation.
Introduces a controlled load session, which is important for progressive overload.
plan_b_advantages: Emphasizes form and cadence, which are beneficial for all runners.
Prioritizes recovery with a higher proportion of rest days.
Potentially less taxing on the body due to the very low intensity of the runs.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates a single aerobic session designed to build endurance, which is crucial for trail running's demands. Plan B, conversely, consists entirely of very short, easy runs with a focus on form, offering minimal stimulus for improving speed or overall fitness. While Plan B prioritizes recovery and good running mechanics, it lacks the necessary volume and intensity to facilitate the desired performance gains. Plan A’s inclusion of a longer aerobic run, even at an easy pace, provides a more effective foundation for building the aerobic capacity required for faster trail running.
